newsitem.title: HUNGARY: German Ruhrgas starts gas supply to MOL.
newsitem.headline: German Ruhrgas starts gas supply to MOL.

text.p: Germany's Ruhrgas AG started supplying Hungarian oil and gas company MOL Rt with natural gas, MOL said on Monday.
"Over the next 10 years five billion cubic metres of gas will arrive to Hungary," MOL said in a statement on Monday.

The shipments will use the recently finished 120 kilometre Hungary-Austria pipeline (HAG) between Baumgarten, eastern Austria and Gyor, north-west Hungary, built by MOL and Austria's OMV, the statement added.

"With this pipeline coming on-line, MOL has started the diversification of its gas supply," the company said, adding that so far, 55 percent of Hungary's annual 11 billion cubic meters gas consumption came from Russia and the rest from domestic sources.
In the first half of 1996, MOL sold natural gas at state-controlled prices that meant a loss of 2.4 forints per cubic metre for the company.
Hungary's government is expected to increase energy prices in January, giving an eight percent return on equity to suppliers.

MOL and Ruhrgas have also signed an agreement by which the German company will help Hungary buy North Sea gas and provide emergency backup in case of technical problems with eastern gas supplies, the statement said.
MOL, with a registered capital of 97.2 billion forints, has the highest capitalisation on the Budapest Stock Exchange, with the state privatisation agency APV Rt the majority owner.
APV holds a 58.7 percent stake and foreign investors own 30.15 percent.
APV Rt announced today that further stakes in MOL will probably be offered next January or February in tranches, as Hungary is trying to maximise revenue from these sales.
